Rule 31: the article governs the expressed head noun θεῷ with a participle following, so it realizes nothing and the supplied relativizer is the participle's helper — θεῷ τῷ δοκιμάζοντι → God who proveth is rule 31's τῷ θεῷ τῷ κτίσαντι → God who created. Rule 90 does not reach it, blessing no unit in which a head noun is expressed; that the head noun is itself anarthrous makes no difference, rule 31's test being whether a head noun is expressed and not whether it carries an article of its own.
δοκιμάζοντι → who proveth, the relativizer being the participle's rule 7 helper under rule 31, headed on the verb word.

Genitive pronoun carries the possessive.
Noun, its determiner slot occupied by our.

review_notes: Corrected s018/s019: the accepted alignment gave who to the article under rule 90, but rule 90 says in terms that it blesses no unit in which a head noun is expressed, and θεῷ is expressed. Rule 31's expressed-head-noun test therefore decides it — the article is unrepresented and who is the participle's helper. This also matches 1TH.2.12's τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ καλοῦντος → God who calleth, which is rule 24's habit.
The remaining articles are decided separately: s005 unrepresented for want of a determiner (rules 21, 23), s020 unrepresented by displacement (rule 20).
καθώς takes even as whole under rule 82; no καί stands in the verse for the bare-even gloss to answer to, and οὕτως keeps its own so.
